brief: A wall-hung spice rack: at least three bins, hung from keyhole hangers.

requirements.evidence: Four cells laid out so the back faces line up on one side for wall mounting. All other faces are capped and the joints are bolted. No props: the catalog has no spice jars.
Four hex-bin-full-div3 bins (3 compartments each) in cells (0,0), (1,0), (1,1) and (2,1).

Two hex-acc-keyhole accessories in slot 1 of the back cells (1,0) and (2,1), which should be in one wall plane by hex layout. Not confirmed: the configurator doesn't report face positions. How much weight they hold depends on the print and the wall screws; the configurator doesn't check load.

finish.summary:
I built a four-cell wall rack. The cells are laid out in a zigzag: two back cells at (1,0) and (2,1), with two front cells at (0,0) and (1,1) sitting between them and slightly further out. Each cell holds a full-depth bin with 3 compartments, so there are 12 spaces for spices.

The rack hangs from two keyhole hangers, one on each back cell, both on the same side (slot 1). I put the cells in a zigzag because a straight row of hex cells has a jagged back with no flat face. Going by the hex layout, the two hanger faces should be in one plane, flat against the wall. The configurator doesn't report face positions, though, so I couldn't confirm that.

All other open faces have solid end caps, and the three joints are bolted (26 parts in total). The build check passed with no rule issues and no mesh collisions. I didn't add any props, because the catalog has no spice jars or anything similar.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
